- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a downward correction of 1–2% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for potential mean reversion or hidden demand.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is low; add a 0.5–1.0% bias upward for first 5–7 days.
- Forecasting horizon >15 days shows increasing lag; adjust for mean reversion by adding 0.3–0.8% downward bias per 5-day lag.
- When sentiment history shows a recent 0.50+ spike, model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance or add 1–2% buffer for uncertainty.
